subject: Judge B: whole-graph wiring recall — propose task→task candidate edges, not just task→note
description:
At wiring time, semantic RAG recall must span the WHOLE graph (notes AND tasks), so an anchor task gets candidate edges to relevant existing TASKS as well as notes — all fed to the judge (task A). Part of the eager-judgment-lifecycle redesign.

This is the PRINCIPLED re-introduction of task→task wiring. Task /5 removed LEXICAL task→task autowire specifically because it had no agent in its lifecycle (never judged). Now tasks carry embeddings (task /7, Step 0), so task→task candidates come from SEMANTIC recall and go through neighborhood-aware JUDGMENT (task A) — an agent fully in the loop. Step /7's task embeddings are the recall substrate for exactly this.

DO:
1. At wiring (autowireNoteProvider's sibling path / the recall that feeds /judge/next), include TASK nodes as candidate providers/consumers for a new anchor task, scored by the same semantic max-cosine over vecs[]. Seed candidate edges at weight 0, by:'autowire', judged:false (existing weight-0 contract) so they are invisible until judged.
2. Do NOT resurrect the lexical scorer for this (Step 1 proved fusion regresses; semantic is the strong signal for recall). Lexical scoreMatches stays only for suggest_links.
3. The judge (task A) then adjudicates these task→task candidates with kind/dup classification.

TEST: a new task semantically near an existing task gets a weight-0 unjudged candidate edge that surfaces on /judge/next; it stays retrieval-invisible until judged; no lexical autowire returns.

GUARDRAIL: surgical; reuse the note-provider recall machinery. Daemon restart to go live (note, do not restart — gated).
